# websocketd

> websocketd wraps an existing command line program and serves it over
> WebSocket. Any program that reads standard input and writes standard
> output becomes a WebSocket server, with no networking code of its own.
> One process is started per connection, so connections share no state
> and there is no built-in broadcast.

The site is organised on the four Diataxis modes. Pick the section by
what you need right now: to be taught (start), to get a job done
(how-to), to look up a fact (reference), or to understand why
(understanding).

For every page concatenated into one document, see /llms-full.txt,
generated at build time from the same content this index describes.

## Start — learning

- /start/ — install, then one lesson that ends with a browser talking to a script
- /start/install/ — get the binary on your PATH, or build it with go build
- /start/tutorial/ — wrap a script, drive it from the dev console, serve your own page

## How-to — doing

- /how-to/ — the three groups below

### Language fixes: a script that streams in a terminal but not under websocketd

- /how-to/languages/ — group index
- /how-to/languages/python/ — python3 -u, or flush after each print
- /how-to/languages/ruby/ — STDOUT.sync = true
- /how-to/languages/nodejs/ — read stdin with readline; output needs no flush
- /how-to/languages/php/ — flush(), ob_flush(), and the <? short-tag trap
- /how-to/languages/c/ — setbuf(stdout, NULL), setvbuf, or fflush
- /how-to/languages/windows-scripts/ — name the interpreter; no shebangs, no signals

### Deployment: running it somewhere

- /how-to/deploy/ — group index
- /how-to/deploy/nginx/ — the two headers nginx drops, and the idle timeout
- /how-to/deploy/apache/ — mod_proxy_wstunnel
- /how-to/deploy/haproxy/ — HTTP-mode backend carrying the upgrade
- /how-to/deploy/systemd/ — a unit that starts at boot and restarts on failure
- /how-to/deploy/docker/ — a container image; no pty, and PID 1 signal handling
- /how-to/deploy/kubernetes/ — Deployment, Service, WebSocket-aware Ingress
- /how-to/deploy/tls/ — wss:// with --ssl, mutual TLS with --sslca, or TLS at a proxy
- /how-to/deploy/share-a-port/ — one public port, two servers
- /how-to/deploy/public-internet/ — checklist before exposing it beyond localhost

### Patterns: problem shapes

- /how-to/patterns/ — group index
- /how-to/patterns/share-state/ — message bus, shared file, or a long-lived backend
- /how-to/patterns/add-auth/ — authenticate at a proxy, or check a token in the script
- /how-to/patterns/run-once/ — a single instance, or a program that stays running
- /how-to/patterns/pass-arguments/ — query string versus --passenv, and why they differ
- /how-to/patterns/debug-a-script/ — drive an endpoint with --devconsole

## Reference — looking up

- /reference/ — section index, and the flag-ordering rule that applies to every flag
- /reference/cli-flags/ — every flag and default, generated from the live flag set
- /reference/environment-variables/ — every variable set for a spawned process, and which the client controls
- /reference/exit-codes/ — every exit code, its trigger, and which stream carries the message
- /reference/dev-console/ — what --devconsole serves, and its response contract
- /reference/platform-support/ — released platforms, and what differs on Windows
- /reference/examples/ — the repository's examples/ directory, per language

## Understanding — why

- /understanding/ — section index
- /understanding/process-model/ — one process per connection, and what it rules out
- /understanding/message-framing/ — the newline boundary, and what --binary changes
- /understanding/output-buffering/ — why runtimes withhold output when stdout is a pipe
- /understanding/process-lifecycle/ — lazy start, and the teardown ladder
- /understanding/cgi-environment/ — request to environment, and the trust boundaries
- /understanding/security-model/ — origin policy, TLS, and why there is no built-in auth
- /understanding/design-decisions/ — no broadcast, no pty, no auth, and what was reverted
